Declared polarity per LTCODE.

WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. Without it a row is either declared lower-is-better in the config or coloured by sign. A resolver that can only answer True or False cannot tell a metric DECLARED higher-is-better from one that merely missed every lookup, so nothing downstream could warn about the second: an undeclared operation-and-maintenance cost line that overspends consensus would grade Beat, in GREEN.

WHAT IT IS FOR. Two things. It gives the resolver a third answer, so 'never established' is distinguishable from 'established as higher-is-better'. And it gives polarity_colour_lint a SECOND SOURCE: the renderer stamps each graded row's ltcode into the HTML as data-lt and the layer resolves polarity from THIS FILE, independently of the renderer's own cue list, so the two can genuinely disagree.

WHAT MAY BE ADDED. Only a code whose label is sourced from this package's own spec - common/sectors.json, the BUILD.md 'Common LTCODEs' cheat-sheet, sector_resolve.py's documented ladder, or a fixture that grades that code (the `source` field names which). A wrong entry silently defeats a correct name-cue and is worse than no entry, so the `source` field is required on every code. _S_ codes are per-ticker and MUST NEVER appear here: the same code is a cost line on one issuer and a profit line on another.

BEHAVIOUR-NEUTRALITY. Every addition must leave the resolved polarity of every (label, code) pair in the fixture corpus unchanged, so the file makes the silence legible without moving a verdict.
